note_claims.claim: Diarrhoea and vomiting for 2 weeks.
Vomited twice this morning, none since lunch.
Four to five loose stools today.
Blood in stools.
Crampy abdominal pain before defecation.
Poor oral intake.
Last passed dark urine this morning.
Postural dizziness.
No falls (the fall mentioned by her son was a neighbour's).
Tired but not confused, per son.
District nurses dressing a sore on the right heel twice weekly.
Metformin 500 mg twice daily.
Ramipril 5 mg once daily.
Furosemide 40 mg each morning (initially said two tablets, corrected to one).
Atorvastatin at night.
Codeine intolerance (vomiting).
Telephone consultation; not examined.
Probable infective gastroenteritis with dehydration in an 85-year-old on metformin, an ACE inhibitor and a loop diuretic; risk of acute kidney injury.
Sick day rules: temporarily stop metformin, ramipril and furosemide until eating and drinking normally for 24–48 hours; continue atorvastatin.
Small, frequent fluids; oral rehydration sachets.
U&E at next routine review.
Call 111 (or 999 if very unwell) if unable to keep fluids down, confused or very drowsy, pass no urine for 12 hours, or blood in stool.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician is calling Mrs Brackenbury.
Patient confirms she is speaking.
Clinician identifies herself as Dr Osei from the surgery and asks if it is alright to talk.
Patient confirms Martin is present and on the speakerphone.
Relative greets the doctor.
Clinician asks Mrs Brackenbury to confirm her date of birth.
Patient's date of birth is March 3, 1941.
Clinician asks what has been happening.
Patient reports having 'the runs' and being sick, feeling 'washed out'.
Clinician asks how long the symptoms have been going on.
Patient states symptoms have been going on for two days, since Monday.
Clinician asks how many times she has been sick today.
Patient reports being sick twice this morning and nothing since lunch.
Clinician asks how many times the diarrhoea has occurred.
Patient reports four or five times today.
Clinician asks if there is any blood in the diarrhoea.
Patient confirms there is no blood.
Clinician asks if she is managing to drink.
Patient reports only sips of water and doesn't fancy much.
Relative reports she has barely touched her tea all day.
Clinician asks when she last passed urine and what colour it was.
Patient states she last passed urine this morning and it was dark.
Clinician asks if she feels dizzy when she stands up.
Patient reports feeling a bit dizzy and holds onto furniture.
Clinician asks if she has had any falls.
Relative mentions she had a fall last month, clarifying it was Mrs Jenkins' fall.
Patient denies falling, stating the fall mentioned was Mrs Jenkins' and she hasn't fallen.
Relative confirms the fall mentioned was Mrs Jenkins' fall.
Clinician asks about tummy pain.
Patient reports feeling crampy before going.
Clinician asks if she is feeling confused and if she seems her usual self.
Relative reports she is tired but making sense.
Clinician asks about her tablets, specifically Metformin.
Patient confirms taking Metformin 500 mg twice a day.
Clinician asks about Ramipril 5 milligrams.
Patient confirms taking Ramipril.
Clinician asks about the water tablet, Furosemide, and how much she takes.
Patient initially stated she takes two tablets in the morning, but corrected to taking one 40 milligram tablet each morning.
Clinician confirms the dose of Furosemide (one 40 milligram tablet each morning) and asks about Atorvastatin.
Patient confirms taking Atorvastatin at night.
Clinician asks about allergies.
Patient reports Codeine intolerance because it makes her very sick.
Clinician asks if anything else is going on, specifically wounds or sores.
Patient states the district nurse dresses a sore on her left heel twice a week.
Clinician suggests the symptoms sound like a tummy bug and expresses concern about dehydration and kidney effects from her medications.
Patient responds with 'Oh dear.'
Clinician instructs the patient to stop Metformin, Ramipril, and Furosemide while unwell, restarting them after 24-48 hours of normal eating/drinking, and continuing Atorvastatin.
Relative agrees to write down the instructions.
Clinician advises trying to drink small amounts often, a few mouthfuls every 10 to 15 minutes, and suggests rehydration sachets.
Patient acknowledges the advice.
Clinician plans a blood test tomorrow to check kidneys and will ask the district nurse to take it when she comes to do the heel dressing.
Relative agrees that the blood test plan is good.
Clinician provides safety-netting instructions: call 111 (or 999 if very unwell) if unable to keep fluids down, confused or very drowsy, pass no urine for 12 hours, or see blood in diarrhoea.
Relative acknowledges the safety instructions and thanks the doctor.
